mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the cost of capital and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The current FEDFUNDS value of 0.14 is below 0.5%, confirming the signal.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signals monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in >50% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, GDP growth (GDPC1) is typically high but market overvaluation leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in >50% of instances during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) signal increased construction activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in >50% of instances when HOUST is rising, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals economic weakness that reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >50% of instances when INDPRO and GDPC1 are rising, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During an inflation shock (CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate > 5.0%), central banks tighten monetary policy, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >50% of instances during inflation shocks (CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate > 5.0%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
